title: There can be equitable social welfare orders but no fair voting system
summary: In the context of intergenerational equity it is natural to ask that social welfare orders have th properties of finite anonymity and strong Pareto efficiency. Such social welfare orders can be constructed from nonprincipal ultrafilters over the set of natural numbers, and the existence of ultrafilters of this kind is known to be equivalent to the existence of a fair voting system for a countably infinite population in the sense of Arrow's theorem.
